speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are here regarding a skin condition; can you describe the appearance, location, and how long the lesions have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and finger. Given the patient's significant history of tobacco use, male gender, and the specific description of "non-healing, red, crusty" lesions in both locations, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of cutaneous SCC. I will now proceed to confirm the diagnosis and staging.
